inShort: A serves for power and depth, and B checks three things: a wide stance, contact out in front and a full turn. 10 serves, then swap.
rules: A serves from the baseline with a bag of balls. B stands beside A.
Stance: wide, like a boxer. Front foot turned about 45° toward the baseline, back foot along it. B gives A a light push from the side; if A wobbles, widen.
Contact: out in front, far enough that A reaches a little for it. Elbow away from the body, not tucked in.
Turn: the paddle side turns away, then through the ball. B checks the finish: the back foot steps into the court, the paddle side ends facing the target. Back foot still on the ground means arm only.
A serves deep cross-court. After 10 serves, swap roles.
tooEasy: 8 of 10 serves land in the back third with the full finish. Even harder: add topspin and aim deeper, because topspin lands shorter.
tooHard: Work one fix at a time, slowly, and use the drop serve only.
goodLooksLike: The back foot steps into the court on the finish, and the serve bounces in the back third of the box.
